safety_bounds.label: Egg coagulation onset
safety_bounds.description: Egg proteins begin to denature and form a gel network around 62 °C. K2 state transitions from liquid → coagulating at this boundary.

safety_bounds.label: Full egg coagulation
safety_bounds.description: Egg proteins fully cross-linked into a firm solid above 70 °C. K2 state transitions from coagulating → solid at this boundary. Irreversible beyond this point.

safety_bounds.label: Maillard browning onset
safety_bounds.description: Maillard reaction between reducing sugars and amino acids begins ~140 °C. Produces browning, flavour changes, and aroma compounds. For scrambled eggs: indicates pan temperature is dangerously high.

safety_bounds.label: Butter smoke point
safety_bounds.description: Unsalted butter smoke point ~150 °C. Clarified butter is higher (~250 °C). Indicates pan is too hot for fat medium.

safety_bounds.label: Syneresis (weeping) risk
safety_bounds.description: Over-contraction of the protein matrix forces liquid out of curds. Caused by over-heating past full coagulation (70 °C+) or mechanical over-agitation of set curds. Not a single temperature; triggered by continuing to cook past solid state.

source_spans: Cook for 60 seconds in total until you have a pile of soft, custardy scrambled egg folds ("curds") and no raw egg leaking on the edges of the pile.
Junte os ovos batidos e deixe cozinhar em lume brando, envolvendo lentamente.
Pour in the eggs, and let them cook for a few seconds without stirring. Pull a rubber spatula across the bottom of the pan to form large, soft curds of scrambled eggs.

Stir the eggs occasionally with a spatula. At first the eggs will be very liquidy; then you'll notice large, opaque curds starting to form. Eventually, the eggs will no longer run in to fill the gaps when you stir. Frequent stirring will give you smaller curds; stirring less frequently will give you larger, irregular curds. Continue cooking until the eggs are as soft or as firm as you like them, about 10 to 15 minutes.
Keep gently stirring until the eggs still look silky, slightly runny and slightly underdone, and then remove from the heat – the heat of the pan will continue to cook the eggs to perfection.
